findings.title: Public auth and filter SQL fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so AND-composition changes which rows match
findings.description:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` (lines 83-88) returns whatever `buildAuthorizationConditions()` produced. For org scope, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` ends with a reduce that yields `(A) OR (B)` with no enclosing parentheses (lines 171-174). Team scope does the same (lines 204-207). `buildFilterConditions` does this too: with only `eventTypeId` set it returns the bare `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` (lines 104-107, 119-122). `getBaseConditions()` only wraps when both auth and filter exist (line 73). With no filters it returns the bare fragment (line 75).

The old code returned nested `{ AND: [{ OR: [...] }] }` objects, so Prisma grouped the OR correctly for any caller. A raw string does not. Take a caller that writes `WHERE ${await service.getAuthorizationConditions()} AND "status" = 'accepted'` for org scope. The text becomes `WHERE (A) OR (B) AND "status" = 'accepted'`. AND binds tighter than OR in PostgreSQL, so the team-booking branch `(A)` skips the `status` filter. The filter case is worse: `WHERE ${await service.getFilterConditions()} AND "userId" = Y` becomes `eventTypeId = X OR (eventParentId = X AND userId = Y)`, which returns every booking of event type X regardless of user.

No code in this repo composes these fragments that way today. `getBaseConditions` wraps the combined case, and the test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` alone. The hazard is still part of the public contract, and the test file locks it in: the org and team expectations at `__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:296-300` and `:333-345` assert the unparenthesized `... OR ...` form.

Suggested fix: wrap each returned fragment in parentheses at the public getters (or at each return point in the builders), for example `Prisma.sql\`(${x})\``, and update the expected values in those tests to match.

structured_findings.summary: Public auth and filter SQL fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so AND-composition changes which rows match
